recipes.name: Patricia's Green Chile Soup
ingredients_raw: 0.5 cup chopped fresh green chile peppers
1 (10.75 ounce) can condensed cream of chicken soup

steps.text: Melt butter in a large saucepan over medium-high heat. Sauté onion and garlic until translucent, 3 to 4 minutes. Add chicken, chiles, and cumin.
Cook until flavors are blended, about 1 minute. Stir in soup, and half-and-half until well combined. Continue to cook until heated through, about 5 minutes.
Ladle soup into bowls; top with cheese, and a dollop of sour cream.

raw_recipe.headline: Patricia's Green Chile Soup
raw_recipe.description: Patricia's green chili soup recipe makes a hearty, spicy meal made with simple refrigerator and pantry staples — it's sure to become a dinner favorite.

review.reviewBody: I doubled the recipe, used roasted, New-Mexican green chilis, added cilantro, salt, a LOT of freshly ground pepper and used Colby-Jack cheese. Very tasty, very easy and very quick! I have already been asked for the recipe and I just served it for the first time a few minutes ago!
Very yummy, but not spicy. I was hoping to recreate Central Market's Green Chili Chicken soup, but this was creamier. I would definitely add something to spice this up.
Very easy to make, used boiled chicken instead of canned. I did use canned green chile's with much success.

I used a pound of chicken breast, which I cubed and sauteed with the onion. I also used about 1 3/4 cup of half & half. I put 2 cans of green chiles into my chopper to make them a bit finer, then I added another can of chiles which I didn't chop. I also added a small bag of potatoes to the soup. It was so good! My husband and I really loved the creamy texture. I will double the recipe next time, however, because between me, my husband, and our 3 older daughters, we ate every drop of this!

A nice mild creamy chili soup that is easy to make for one or two people. You could easily add in extra spices or herbs and maybe even a can of beans if you desire. I put in one chopped jalapeno pepper and some shakes of Mexican oregano, and dried parsley for some extra flavor. I was delighted to see other reviews that used canned green chilies since fresh are not in the markets this time of year. I let it gently simmer for about an hour to allow for the flavors to release. I'm sure I'll make it again and hopefully have fresh chilies next time, although it was very good with the canned chilies.
MMmmm... this was really tasty. However, my husband and I had this as a meal and it was barely enough. I would double it next time, and use twice as much chicken - just a little skimpy.

I used this recipe to create a vegetarian version. I followed the recipe as written except for the following: First, I used one can of cream of celery soup and two stalks of chopped celery. I substituted diced potatoes for the chicken. I also added a can of chopped green chiles to the two small fresh roasted chiles I had. I also used regular milk (enough to fill the soup can) and 2 cups of vegetable broth. To the cumin I added dried cilantro, oregano, and smoked paprika. I cooked it about a half hour, added the sour cream right into the soup, and omitted the cheese. It turned out delicious. Thanks for the recipe, Patricia!

Good recipe. I used grilled chicken breasts instead of canned and some diced tomato as well. It worked okay with regular milk instead of half-n-half. I would recommend it. Nice served with the buttered tortillas.

Delicious soup - reminds me of Chicken enchiladas.
Both of my teenagers loved it. I doubled the recipe thinking it didn't seem like much, but it is so rich, I think the proportions are probably about right for each serving. We love spicy, so I added some diced jalepenos.

This is a family favorite. I double or even triple the recipe, use Anaheim peppers (about double the amount called for) and about a half a jalapeno. I sauté the peppers with the garlic and onion to get them nice and soft. Get it to a nice slow simmer and dump in about 1 and 1/2 the cheese (I use Monterey Jack). Serve with warm tortillas or garlic bread. We love it.

This was most excellent! My wife who still can't taste or smell much post covid, said it was delicious, and I can "feel free to make it again anytime". That's huge. I cubed a chicken breast and sauteed it with the onions and garlic. Replaced a lot of the half and half with 2% milk, and the other posters were right, it was still plenty creamy with the cream of chicken soup. I did add some oregano and ground black pepper, also. Snuck in a half cup of frozen corn at the end, because my trophy wife likes it in almost everything. The Hatch chilis gave it just the right touch of heat.
I made this soup exactly as written! Shared it with my neighbors and we ALL thought it was delicious! Perfect for Fall weather, but will definitely be making it year round!!

I thought it sounded great but had stew meat on hand vs chicken so I used that and cream of mushroom instead. I think cream of celery would’ve also been good. I also added cilantro while cooking as well as garnished with it afterwards. I also used lime flavored tortilla chips with mine and so did my boyfriend. All in all, it was a super easy hit for my family. Not too spicy but still so flavorful.

Fantastic and easy soup, thanks, Patricia for posting it. I used some left-over rotisserie chicken and canned green chilis since that's what I had and substituted skim milk for the half and half and it was still yummy, I can only imagine how great it would have been with 1/2 and 1/2!

Great recipe, thank you! I have made it 3 times now and it's one of my favorite soups. I use cut up boneless skinless chicken thighs, about 1-1/2 or 2 per 1X recipe, and just cook them in the soup. Also I vary the chiles, sometimes fresh jalapeno, sometimes pickled jalapeno, sometimes canned green chiles (still pretty good) depending on what's available. A tablespoon of black pepper, a little salt, and I don't bother with the cheese or sour cream because the soup is already pretty decadent:)
I just made it. It is bland. I added taco seasoning more cumin and black pepper. I did use canned diced green peppers and fresh chicken. I don't like spicy things.

I made some changes to the recipe because I was out of onion and cream of chicken soup.
I substituted store bought pico de gallo for the onion. I substituted cream of mushroom soup for the cream of chicken. 
It tastes delicious. 
I'm making chicken quesadillas to go with the soup for dinner on this cold evening.
I added 14 oz of canned chicken and 2% milk instead. Delicious
I use this soup as the topping for my chicken enchiladas. Very good!
Can’t wait to take it to the chili party tomorrow!!!!! Yummm
